summary: Reports statistics gathered by the NIC's NCP implementation over roughly 100 hours of uptime: counts of incoming messages, host-host control messages and the sizes of outgoing messages. The author suggests that people building NCPs for servers should consider the results.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC reports statistics collected by the NIC's NCP over about 100 hours of operation. It uses the observed message patterns to suggest design priorities for NCP implementations.

questions: what kinds of messages did early ncp servers see
how big were early arpanet messages
subtitle: Message and opcode statistics from the NIC's NCP experiment.

tldr.problem: NCP implementers needed evidence about the messages and control operations handled during network use.
tldr.mechanism: The NIC collected incoming-message, incoming-control-opcode, and outgoing-message-size statistics over about 100 hours of uptime.
tldr.outcome: The author uses the results to recommend efficient control-message handling and attention to both small and large messages.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 550's status as Unknown. The RFC reports an NCP experiment and recommendations based on its observations.

sections.title: Collecting NCP Statistics
sections.content:
The NIC NCP kept statistics for about 100 hours of uptime, most of it during the working day. It counted incoming messages, incoming host-host control opcodes, and the sizes of outgoing messages.

The author presents the results qualitatively because the counters were reset each time the system came up.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC's NCP counted messages and control operations during about 100 hours online. The data is approximate because counters reset when the system restarted.

sections.title: Message and Opcode Patterns
sections.content:
The RFC says incoming and outgoing message totals were almost identical, with about 5% more outgoing messages. Slightly more than half as many incoming control opcodes were processed as incoming messages; assuming at most one opcode per control message, the author infers that slightly more than half of incoming messages were control messages.

ALL made up most opcode counts, ranging from about 50% on weekends to 98% on a busy weekday. The RFC also says 95% of outgoing messages carried 1 to 4 PDP-10 words of data.
sections.plainLanguage: Incoming and outgoing message counts were close. Control opcodes were common, and most outgoing messages contained only a few PDP-10 words of data.

sections.title: Implications for NCP Design
sections.content:
The author recommends that NCPs process control messages efficiently because they form a large share of messages. Since most messages are short, he says elaborate buffering and queuing might not be worthwhile if their host overhead outweighs benefits.

He also notes that a meaningful share of outgoing data was in larger messages, so NCPs must handle these efficiently rather than always sending very short messages.
sections.plainLanguage: NCPs should handle common control messages efficiently and avoid unnecessary overhead for short messages. They must also handle larger messages effectively.
